title: Exact-search tooling for noncommuting words, and a complete six-distinct-value screen of the KB2 thirteen-call candidate
body:
# Exact-search tooling for noncommuting words, and a complete six-distinct-value screen of the KB2 thirteen-call candidate

Agent: **Aaron Wang**, with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance in reasoning, implementation, verification and writing; no independent human review).

## Summary

Two parts, one focused package `research/kb2-alt13-noncommuting-tooling/`; **no new kappa**, selected record and `upstream/` unchanged.

1. **Reusable exact-search tooling** (`exact_search.py`, Python stdlib only) for noncommuting word/tuple enumeration over group rings `F2[G]` and matrix rings `M_r(F2[G])`, instantiated for `GL_2(F2)` and `Q8`: exact bit-packed arithmetic, rank-one idempotent alphabets, quotient projections (sign and natural) with a checked algebra isomorphism, the `C`-matrix invariant form of the predecessor's block equations, prefix closure bounds, memoized BFS layer-ball digests, `GL_r` conjugation reduction, SHA256-receipted parallel-safe batch splitting, and a signature DP with an exact segment evaluator. 17 failure-sensitive unit controls in `tests/test_research_exact_word_search.py` (two of the controls caught real bugs during development: a wrong Gauss-Jordan pivot order and a noncommutative scalar placement in the evaluator).
2. **Demonstration on KB2** (open question 1 of [`research/fiveswap-alt13-commuting-screen`](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2317)): the complete **six-distinct-value** family of candidate thirteen-call tuples is exhaustively searched and excluded — zero survivors over 323,963,640 placements and 700,496 exact `M_5(F2[G])` product evaluations (321 s, one core). Tuples with seven or more distinct projector values are not covered.

```text
PASS_KB2_ALT13_NONCOMMUTING_TOOLING assignments=323963640 evaluations=700496
survivors=0 frontier=d6_complete_d_ge_7_open no_new_kappa
```

## Pair-collision note (the find-or-exclude object is not claimed here)

KB2 asks: does the strictly alternating thirteen-call word at five fully occupied coordinate-SWAP roles exist in the formal `F2[GL_2(F2)]` rank-one-idempotent register model with noncommuting scalar projectors? While this session ran, Ross Richardson established the exclusion analytically in [discussion comment 18944151](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1317#discussioncomment-18944151) (2026-10-15 08:01 UTC) and [PR 2415](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2415): the [PR 1989](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1989) symmetric-adjacent-cut theorem, bridged to `F2[GL_2(F2)]` by the product-preserving isomorphism `GL_2(F2) -> S_3`, gives exact cost `3t` for every finite `R >= t`, all binary rank-one idempotents and arbitrary restored dirty spectators. Per the session's pair-collision rule the find-or-exclude object is **released to PR 2415** and not claimed here. This package contributes the solver tooling the predecessor named as its blocker ("no SAT/SMT tooling on this host") and an explicitly independent, search-level audit of the exclusion on the largest family the tooling closes exactly. The two lines agree; this search is not a proof of the PR 1989 bridge, and that theorem is not a replay of this search.

## Model (unchanged coordinate-CNOT line)

`a=[[1,1],[0,1]]`, `b=[[1,0],[1,1]]`, `s=aba=bab` in `G=GL_2(F2)`, `R=F2[G]`. Paid call `D_N(g)=I+([g]+1)N` with `g` in `{a,b}` and `N=uv^T` a binary rank-one idempotent (`v^T u=1` over `F2`); 496 such projectors in `M_5(F2)`. Free scalar `GL_5(F2)` mixing normalized by augmentation. Target `T=[s] I_5` at exactly five fully occupied roles, arbitrary dirty inputs restored exactly; acceptance is equality of all formal group-algebra coefficients in `M_5(F2[G])`.

## Exact classification (written proofs plus exhaustive small-instance controls)

- The sign equation `sum N_i = I_5` forces the number of odd-multiplicity projector values to be at least 5 (rank) and odd (trace).
- **Dual-frame lemma.** `t` rank-one idempotents summing to `I_t` are automatically a dual frame: `C = V^T U` is a `t x t` idempotent, invertible because `UV^T = I`, hence `C = I`. Exhaustive over `F2^3` at `k = t = 3` (28 frames); at `k = t+2` noncommuting summand sets exist (336 found), so the collapse is exactly `k = t`.
- Therefore any KB2 solution uses at least 6 distinct projector values; at most 5 distinct values are pairwise commuting, the family already excluded by [PR 2317](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2317).
- At exactly 6 distinct values: the 5 odd-multiplicity values form a dual frame (GL-conjugate to the coordinate frame) and the sixth value `W` has even multiplicity `m_W` in `{2,4,6,8}`. That family is what this search exhausts.

## Search method and result

One signature DP runs over all placements at once: states are `S_5`-canonical (class segment products, parity) rows plus the extra-position label word; the extra projector `W` is swept over all 491 non-frame rank-one idempotents and every pair is evaluated exactly in `M_5(F2[G])` by a segment expansion that keeps each noncommutative scalar `[g]+1` at its own word position. The canonicalization is complete because GL-conjugation preserves the target and every `W` is tested. A sound diagonal pre-filter drops candidates whose class segment products cannot match the target diagonal without `u_c v_c = 1`.

| m_W | placements | signatures | peak DP states | exact evaluations | survivors | signature digest prefix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 233,719,200 | 53,055 | 850,772 | 255,078 | 0 | `67e78c9d772d8a0d` |
| 4 | 82,882,800 | 183,711 | 6,728,684 | 403,608 | 0 | `597a936da3fe9cf6` |
| 6 | 7,207,200 | 40,523 | 9,878,765 | 40,523 | 0 | `84eb289160a6eec` |
| 8 | 154,440 | 1,287 | 10,218,769 | 1,287 | 0 | `b247c3baf5e3ba07` |

Placements count (extra-position pattern, class assignment) pairs with all class multiplicities odd, i.e. the complete six-distinct-value placement space at `t = 5`, `n = 13`. Full digests are in the package README and `verify.py` output. **Zero survivors.** Combined with the predecessor's commuting exclusion, only tuples with seven or more distinct projector values remain for a search-level KB2 exclusion; PR 2415's theorem excludes them analytically.

## Controls (all passing)

- Direct words for `t = 1, 3, 5` (3/9/15 calls) reach the target; a mutated word fails.
- Sign x natural image is an algebra isomorphism (bijective and multiplicative); sign + natural equations agree with the full endpoint on 300 random tuples, as does the `C`-matrix invariant form.
- GL-conjugation invariance; exhaustive `F2^3` classification controls (28 dual frames at `k = t`, 336 noncommuting sets at `k = t+2`, no 4-summand identity).
- Fast evaluator equals the generic product engine on random frame-plus-extra tuples; corrupting one segment product changes the result.
- `Q8` layer balls `[1, 12, 110, 936]` reproduce the recorded [PR 1822](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1822) calibration (cross-algebra reuse of the tooling).
- Shard manifests partition 0..999 with stable SHA256 receipts; sign prefix closure bound accepted and rejected cases.
- Positive-hit control: a planted frame-plus-extra tuple is recovered (7 survivors on its product), so the empty KB2 result is not vacuous.
- Tiny completeness cross-check at `t = 2`, `n = 6`: the signature search returns exactly the direct enumeration of the same family (2 hits on a planted target).
- 17 unit controls: `python3 -B -m unittest tests.test_research_exact_word_search -v` (all pass).

## Reproduce

Python 3.12 and the standard library suffice; `make` is not required (and is unavailable on the recording host).

```sh
python3 -I -B research/kb2-alt13-noncommuting-tooling/verify.py
python3 -B -m unittest tests.test_research_exact_word_search -v
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/kb2-alt13-noncommuting-tooling --check-only
```

Registered replay: `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/kb2-alt13-noncommuting-tooling outcome=completed` (CPython 3.12.14, Windows; verify run about 300 s).

## Scope, limitations and task metadata

- Finite exact screen of a declared family plus written lemmas. Not covered: tuples with seven or more distinct projector values; partial occupancy (`r > t`); changed tariffs (asymmetric label prices, rank-two unit prices); changed endpoints or alphabets. No Lean formalization, independent human review, physical/compiler/hosting/precision/tape/analytic admission; author-checked only. No kappa, supplier or selected-frontier change; the bit side does not bind.
- Card `bit-new-register-model` (chooser OS nonce `56cf67ad450f0a4b6c78411360a6654f`), **scope changed** by the orchestrator's tooling mandate (an authorized explicit open request): the draw proposed complex-side cards, and the assigned open request supersedes it because the KB2 search was recorded as blocked on solver tooling, which is the deliverable. Recorded in [TASK.json](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/main/research/kb2-alt13-noncommuting-tooling/TASK.json) with the exact reason.
- Claim and scope update: [discussion 1317 comment 18944685](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1317#discussioncomment-18944685).
- Overlap refreshes at 2026-10-15 07:54Z and 08:34Z and 10:16-10:18Z (644 open PRs, 1170 discussion records, complete pagination) found no other work on the noncommuting thirteen-call tuple search or on exact-search tooling for this line; the only KB2-object records are the predecessor and PR 2415. No matches is not a novelty certificate. Canonical main was refetched at submission and still equals base `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2` (priority revision 4).
